text: Write a method whose name is a promise and whose body could be replaced entirely. Fill in the two blanks so both implementations pass the same check.
choices: System.out.println(___);            // the promise the name makes
explanation: Verified: 3, then true. A loop over `toCharArray` would satisfy the same check, which is the point — the name states what is guaranteed and the body is an implementation detail the caller must not depend on. Chapter 35 calls this the second of the book's two ideas: an abstraction's value is not what is behind it but what it lets you stop thinking about.
